# Lightning PM API

Use the authenticated API instead of scraping HTML.

- Base API: `/api/v1`
- Auth: `Authorization: Bearer <api_key>` or `X-LPM-API-Key: <api_key>`
- Current user: `GET /api/v1/me`
- List projects: `GET /api/v1/projects` (add `?archive=1` for archived)
- Resolve issue by pasted URL: `GET /api/v1/issues/resolve?url=<issue_url>`
- Load issue by id: `GET /api/v1/issues/{issueId}`
- Create issue: `POST /api/v1/issues` (name must have a title besides `[label]` prefixes; some projects require at least one label; `priority` is the `1..100` value shown in the UI, default `50`; optional `board`: `true` puts the new issue on the scrum board by its status, a column key puts it in that column)
- Add comment: `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/comments`
- List project issues: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/issues` (filters: `status`, `type`, `label`, `search`, `limit`, `offset`)
- List project labels (tags): `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/labels` (sorted by usage in this project)
- Read project scrum board: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/board` (issues grouped by columns `todo`, `inProgress`, `testing`, `done`, in board order; `400` for a non-scrum project)
- Put issue on the board / move between columns: `PUT /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/board` (optional `column` from the same set; without it the column follows the issue status, as the «На доску» button does; `testing` sends the issue to test, `done` completes it)
- Take issue off the board: `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/board` (issue returns to the backlog, status unchanged)
- List repositories: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/repositories`
- List branches: `GET /api/v1/projects/{projectId}/repositories/{repositoryId}/branches`
- Create branch: `POST /api/v1/issues/{issueId}/branches`

The issue payload reports its board position as `isOnBoard` and `boardColumn` (`null` for an issue in the backlog).

Attachments come in the issue payload as `files` (attached to the issue) and `comments[].files` (attached to a comment), both with the same item shape `{fileId, uid, name, mimeType, size, sizeFormatted, created, url, requiresAuthentication}`. A `url` with `requiresAuthentication: true` needs the same auth header as any other request.

Comments should be high-signal only: use them for tester instructions, caveats, or implementation details not already clear from the issue. Do not post routine progress updates such as branch creation or "implementation started".

An issue URL of this instance written in a description or a comment automatically links the two issues.
